subject: Milestone‑triggered discounts and surplus credit schedule
messages:
From: Laurence Chen <laurence.chen@brightcart.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: 2025-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing for launch month spikes + commit structure

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. BrightCart is planning a Q4 product launch and we expect a large burst in traffic the first 8 weeks. We like the idea of a monthly commit (per‑token) with built‑in flex for launch spikes. A few things procurement asked me to confirm:

- Can discounts be tied to cumulative monthly milestones instead of a flat monthly bucket? (e.g., 0–2B tokens = 0% discount, hitting 2B tokens triggers +6% on subsequent tokens, hitting 5B triggers +12% for remainder of month)
- Do you support surplus credits/one‑time burst credits if we exceed forecasted spikes? How are those applied to billing?
- We may need a 30–60 day ramp with smaller commits in month 1–2 and then step‑up commits month 3 onward. Can the contract reflect step increases without renegotiating pricing?

I've attached a quick forecast (BrightCart_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx). Procurement would like a clear example invoice showing how milestone discounts and a surplus credit would appear.

Appreciate any concrete examples you can provide this week — procurement wants to include the numbers in their vendor comparison next Thursday.

Best,
Laurence Chen
Head of Product Partnerships
BrightCart

Attachment: BrightCart_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for launch month spikes + commit structure

Laurence — great to meet you yesterday, and thanks for the forecast. High level: we can structure monthly commits with milestone‑based escalators and a one‑time surplus credit pool for launch spikes. Below is a concrete proposal and an invoice example (summary). I kept the math simple so procurement can plug in your numbers.

Proposal (summary):
- Base monthly commit: 1.5B tokens at $0.0028/token
- Milestone tiers (cumulative within month):
  • 0–2B: no discount (base price)
  • 2B–5B: additional 6% discount applied to incremental tokens above 2B
  • >5B: additional 12% discount applied to incremental tokens above 5B
- Surplus credit: one pooled credit equal to 10% of the monthly commit value (applies as an invoice credit only for the month of the launch spike; unused credits do not roll forward)
- Step‑up commits: allow non‑penalized increases in committed volume on the first of each month with a 2‑week notice; pricing ladder remains intact for new commit level
- True‑up: final invoice performs a true‑up at month end; milestone discounts are applied to actual usage slices retroactively so the invoice reflects the correct discounted bands

Example invoice (month of launch):
- Base commit: 1.5B tokens @ $0.0028 = $4,200
- Usage: 6.3B tokens total
  • First 2B @ $0.0028 = $5,600
  • Next 3B (2B–5B) @ $0.0028 * 0.94 = $7,896
  • Remaining 1.3B @ $0.0028 * 0.88 = $3,212.8
- Subtotal usage charges = $16,708.8
- Surplus credit (10% of commit value = $420) applied against subtotal -> $16,288.8
- Any pre‑paid commit credits applied -> final balance due

Behavioral notes:
- Credits apply after milestone discounts; credits are not tokenized or added to commit buckets — they are invoice credits only.
- If margin concerns require, we can cap the effective discount exposure by setting a monthly surplus credit ceiling or reducing the credit percentage.

I've attached an updated PDF proposal with this layout and the sample invoice (redwood_proposal_v2.pdf). If procurement wants the invoice in CSV for their model, Ben can export a line‑level breakdown.

Would Laurence and procurement accept the 10% one‑time surplus credit and the milestone bands above as the initial structure? If yes, we'll draft contract language and a simple addendum for month‑to‑month step increases.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-30T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pricing for launch month spikes + commit structure

Quick internal — the structure looks fine but margin impact needs the following guardrails:

1) Surplus credit ceiling: recommend max credit = 15% of commit value (we currently proposed 10% so OK)
2) Max retroactive exposure: cap cumulative discount exposure at 20% of billed amount for any single month (prevents large downward adjustments)
3) Require minimum 1‑month notice for contract termination to avoid churn abuse during spikes

If Stephanie wants to give procurement a clean example, I can generate a CSV with token slices and the effective blended rate under different spike scenarios (2x, 3x, 5x forecast).

— Ben
Director, Revenue Ops
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-30T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pricing for launch month spikes + commit structure

Ben — agree with ceilings. Also suggest a phased discount activation for month‑over‑month step increases: first step‑up month gets 50% of the band discount, full band discount applies from month 2 at the new commit level. This limits first‑month leakage when customers suddenly increase committed capacity.

If procurement signs up for the 30‑60 day ramp (1.5B -> 3B -> 5B), the language could read: 
- Month N (step up): effective band discount = 50% of listed band discount for incremental tokens above prior commit
- Month N+1 onward: full band discount for incremental tokens at new commit

I'll let Ben's CSV reflect both immediate and phased band math.

— Aditya
Senior Finance Analyst
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Laurence Chen <laurence.chen@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: 2025-07-01T10:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for launch month spikes + commit structure

Laurence — attached is a line‑level CSV and a sample invoice that shows the phased step‑up behavior Aditya suggested and Ben's proposed ceilings. Key clarifications:

- Surplus credit remains 10% of commit value by default; credit ceiling set at 15% unless BrightCart requests higher in writing.
- If BrightCart step‑ups mid‑month, the 50% phased discount applies for the first month of the increase; full discounts apply from the next billing cycle.
- True‑up calculations are retroactive on usage bands; however, total discount exposure for the month will never exceed 20% of the month’s billed amount (post‑credits).

If that works for procurement, I can circulate draft contract language and an amendment template that supports month‑to‑month step increases with the notice periods.

Would procurement like us to lock in the base commit price for 6 months (to avoid per‑token inflation adjustments)? We can offer fixed unit price for 6 or 12 months — prices above reflect a 6‑month price lock.

— Stephanie
